title: Rate Day
briefing: The central bank decides on interest rates on day 14. A rate-sensitive utility, a high-growth cloud firm and a grocery chain will not react the same way.
objective: Macro surprises move the whole market; rate-sensitive sectors move most.
debrief: Economists expected a 0.25 percentage-point rise; on day 14 the central bank raised rates by 0.50 points. Tidal Power, a heavy borrower, and Nimbus Cloud, priced for distant growth, gapped down and kept falling for days. Orchard Foods, a defensive grocer, barely moved. Cooler inflation on day 23 brought a partial rebound. A disciplined player kept positions moderate before the decision and leaned on the defensive stock.

news.headline: Central bank decides on day 14; most economists expect a 0.25 percentage-point rise
news.body: A larger rise would make borrowing more expensive across the economy.

news.headline: Central bank raises rates by 0.50 percentage points, twice the expected rise
news.body: The bank says inflation is not falling fast enough.

news.headline: Inflation cools more than expected
news.body: Consumer prices rose 2.6% from a year ago, below the 3.0% forecast.

basic.text: Keep every position at or under 25% of your portfolio before the day-14 decision
Hold defensive Orchard Foods through the decision (days 12 to 16)
